title: Coefficient-root polynomial cover of a finite purely inseparable extension
statement: Let R be an integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let F be Frac(R[X]) [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and assume F has prime characteristic p [def-pc-field-characteristic]. Let L/F be a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There exists a finite field extension E/Frac(R) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with compatible R-algebra structure, a positive integer q, and a field embedding f:L → Frac(A[T]), where A is the integral closure of R in E [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], such that on R[X] the map is substitution X ↦ T^q and the canonical coefficient map R → A. Equivalently, f(algebraMap R[X] L a) equals the image in Frac(A[T]) of eval₂(C ∘ algebraMap R A, T^q, a) for every a in R[X]. All fields are in the universe of R. No normality, Noetherian or Japanese hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: Put K = Frac(R) and F = Frac(R[X]). Clearing coefficient denominators identifies F with K(x): every polynomial over K becomes a polynomial over R after multiplication by a common nonzero denominator. The characteristic of F restricts to K. Take a finite F-basis of L. For each basis element pure inseparability gives a p-power in F; take the largest exponent to obtain a common q = p^e. Write these powers as quotients of polynomials over K.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: In an algebraic closure of L choose the unique q-th roots of the finitely many coefficients of the numerator and denominator polynomials. The K-algebra they generate is spanned by monomials with each root exponent below q, because each q-th power is in K. It is finite dimensional and a domain, hence is a field E. Adjoin a root t of t^q=x in the same algebraic closure. For each basis element y, taking coefficient roots in its numerator and denominator produces a quotient z in E(t) with z^q=y^q. Its denominator is nonzero since its q-th power is the original nonzero denominator. Frobenius injectivity gives z=y. Thus all of L embeds in E(t) over F. The field E has the induced compatible R- and K-algebra structures and is finite over K.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: The element t is transcendental over E: otherwise, since E/K is finite, t and therefore x=t^q would be algebraic over K. Let A be the integral closure of R in E. The finite-extension fraction-field lemma identifies E with Frac(A), so clearing coefficient denominators identifies Frac(A[T]) with E(T). Evaluation at the transcendental t identifies E(T) with E(t). Compose L into E(t) with the inverse of this evaluation map to obtain f. Its restriction to R[X] sends coefficients to their constant images in A[T] and X to T^q, yielding precisely the displayed ring-map equation. Algebraic closures, their subfields, polynomial rings and fraction fields all preserve the universe u. The trivial extension uses E=K and q=1.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_purelyInseparable_polynomial_cover
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) p]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) L]
    [Algebra (Polynomial R) L] [IsScalarTower (Polynomial R) (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) L]
    [FiniteDimensional (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) L]
    [IsPurelyInseparable (FractionRing (Polynomial R)) L] :
    ∃ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E) (_ : Algebra (FractionRing R) E) (_ : Algebra R E)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R (FractionRing R) E) (_ : FiniteDimensional (FractionRing R) E),
    ∃ q : ℕ, 0 < q ∧
      ∃ f : L →+* FractionRing (Polynomial (integralClosure R E)),
        ∀ a : Polynomial R,
          f (algebraMap (Polynomial R) L a) =
            algebraMap (Polynomial (integralClosure R E))
              (FractionRing (Polynomial (integralClosure R E)))
              (Polynomial.eval₂RingHom
                (Polynomial.C.comp (algebraMap R (integralClosure R E)))
                (Polynomial.X ^ q) a)
